text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyMercury Has Gotten Smaller Than We ThoughtThe first planet from the sun has been hiding its wrinklesJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on September 15, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleMercury is roughly 100 million miles closer to Earth than Mars, but it takes a lot longer to get there. For example, NASA’s MESSENGER space probe launched in 2004 but didn’t insert into an orbit around Mercury until 2011. The 2005 Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, on the other hand, was whizzing around Mars less than a year after launch. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 A closer look at the ocean's Lost City and life beyond EarthShareNextStayWhy? Well, the sun’s massive gravity well prevents a straight shot—the spacecraft would be traveling too fast to decelerate. So instead MESSENGER had to circle around several times, using the gravity of Earth and Venus to slow down and spiral in. Once in place, the probe performed a series of highly elliptical flybys, mapping the surface of the first planet from the sun. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
